title: CoRD: Combining Raid and Delta for Fast Partial Updates in Erasure-Coded Storage Clusters
problem: Erasure-coded storage systems suffer from expensive update traffic, especially for partial updates. RAID-based schemes incur significant network traffic for partial-block-updates, while Delta-based schemes cannot efficiently share computed-delta parts across partial-stripe-updates.
motivation: Reducing update traffic in erasure-coded storage clusters is critical for improving performance and reducing network overhead in production systems.
method: CoRD combines two storage update approaches—RAID (which uses parity for recovery) and Delta (which tracks just what changed). It identifies places where multiple updated blocks overlap in where they store data (offset address intersections), then sends only the changed parts to update the parity information. For updates spanning multiple blocks, it changes which blocks it uses for parity calculations to reduce network traffic.
key_novelty: The core idea is leveraging offset address intersections—where multiple blocks being updated overlap in memory—to optimally combine RAID and Delta approaches, reducing update traffic for both partial-block and partial-stripe updates.
contributions: Analysis showing partial updates are common in production storage traces
Hybrid CoRD scheme combining RAID and Delta update mechanisms
Offset intersection exploitation to minimize transmitted data
Cross-block optimization through selective block flipping
primary_theme: Optimizing partial updates in erasure-coded storage
